name: SELF_TEST_post
prose: Runs the FIPS module power-on self tests (or re-runs them on demand) and moves the module to the running state on success. Precondition: st holds the module checksum data, file name and BIO callbacks (checked below, except that st is read after the lock); on_demand_test is non-zero when a re-test is requested. It first runs the one-time lock initialisation (failure returns 0). Before taking the lock: if the state is RUNNING and this is not an on-demand test it returns 1; any state other than RUNNING or SELFTEST raises PROV_R_INVALID_STATE and returns 0; these early returns do not change the module error state. It then takes the self-test write lock (failure returns 0). Under the lock it re-reads the state: RUNNING without on-demand unlocks and returns 1, RUNNING with on-demand switches the state to SELFTEST, anything other than SELFTEST unlocks, raises PROV_R_INVALID_STATE and returns 0. Then, with FIPS POST compiled in, it requires st and its checksum data (else PROV_R_MISSING_CONFIG_DATA), creates a self-test event object (failure returns 0), decodes the checksum (PROV_R_INVALID_CONFIG_DATA on failure), verifies the module file integrity (PROV_R_MODULE_INTEGRITY_FAILURE), runs the known-answer tests (PROV_R_SELF_TEST_KAT_FAILURE) and checks that the private RNG was restored (a missing TEST-RAND or an RNG still named TEST-RAND is PROV_R_SELF_TEST_KAT_FAILURE). On success the state becomes RUNNING and it returns 1; on any of these failures it sets the module error state (ossl_set_error_state) and returns 0. The lock is released and temporary objects and the module BIO freed on the paths after the lock was taken. Without FIPS POST it just sets RUNNING, unlocks and returns 1.

Original reviewer partly right: the early returns at 329-330, 337-339 and 342-343 do not set the error state, but no lock is held there (taken only at 342), and the invalid-state return inside the lock (353-356) does unlock. Round-15 reviewer right: OSSL_SELF_TEST_new failure goes to end and returns 0 (365-367, 411-417).

name: rsa_decrypt
prose: RSA asymmetric cipher decrypt operation of the provider. Precondition: vprsactx is a PROV_RSA_CTX with an RSA key; outlen is non-NULL; in holds inlen bytes. Returns 0 at once if the provider is not running. If out is NULL it is a size query: in TLS padding mode it sets *outlen to SSL_MAX_MASTER_KEY_LENGTH and returns 1; in other modes it raises PROV_R_INVALID_KEY and returns 0 if the RSA size is 0, else sets *outlen to the RSA size and returns 1. Otherwise outsize must be at least SSL_MAX_MASTER_KEY_LENGTH (TLS padding) or the RSA size, else PROV_R_BAD_LENGTH and 0. For OAEP and TLS padding it decrypts into a temporary buffer with no padding (returning 0 without an error raised here if the allocation fails, and PROV_R_FAILED_TO_DECRYPT and 0 if the raw decryption does not return the full RSA size), then removes the padding: OAEP uses the label, the OAEP digest (fetching SHA-1 if none is set, 0 with ERR_R_INTERNAL_ERROR if that fails) and the MGF1 digest; TLS padding needs client_version > 0 (else PROV_R_BAD_TLS_CLIENT_VERSION and 0) and uses the TLS type 2 check with the client and alternative versions. The temporary buffer is freed on all these paths. Other padding modes decrypt directly into out with RSA_private_decrypt (PKCS#1 v1.5 without implicit rejection when implicit_rejection is 0). In the decrypting cases the final result r is handled in constant time: *outlen is set to r if r is not negative and left unchanged otherwise, and the function returns 1 if r is not negative and 0 if it is negative. Success therefore includes a decrypted length of 0.

name: aes_get_ctx_params
prose: Reports the AES-CBC-HMAC-SHA cipher context parameters requested in params. Precondition: vctx is a PROV_AES_HMAC_SHA_CTX; params is an OSSL_PARAM array. For each parameter present it writes a value and stops at the first failing one, raising PROV_R_FAILED_TO_SET_PARAMETER and returning 0 (earlier parameters in the array may already have been filled). With multiblock support compiled in it provides the multiblock maximum buffer size (asked from the hardware method), the interleave, the AAD packet length and the encrypted length; it also provides, when requested, the TLS AAD padding (tls_aad_pad), key length, IV length, the original IV (oiv) and the updated IV (iv). The two IV parameters are first tried as a copied octet string of ivlen bytes; if that fails they are tried as an octet pointer, in which case the caller receives a pointer into the context (the address of the oiv or iv array), not a copy. Returns 1 if every parameter that is present was set, including the case where none is present.

name: tls1_multi_block_encrypt
prose: Encrypts one large TLS 1.1+ application record as 4*n4x (n4x is 1 or 2) interleaved fragments with AES-CBC and HMAC-SHA1 using the multi-block assembly routines. Precondition: the context holds the key schedule, the MAC key states (md/tail) and the 13-byte AAD set by the multiblock AAD control; inp holds inp_len bytes; out has room for all fragments, each laid out as a 5-byte record header, a 16-byte explicit IV, the data, a 20-byte MAC and 1..16 padding bytes. Returns 0 if drawing 16*4*n4x random IV bytes with RAND_bytes_ex fails (nothing written). Otherwise it splits the input into x4 fragments of size frag (the last of size last, adjusted so the hash blocks line up), writes each IV before its fragment, computes the HMAC-SHA1 of every fragment in parallel starting from the saved inner state, with the sequence number incremented by the fragment index and the length field rewritten to that fragment length, while CBC-encrypting the data in chunks of up to 2048 bytes, then finishes the inner hash with padding, runs the outer hash, copies the remaining plaintext, appends the MAC and the padding, writes each 5-byte record header (type and version bytes from the AAD, length including the IV, MAC and padding) and finally runs the last CBC pass. It cleanses the temporary hash blocks and context, stores the total number of output bytes in ctx->multiblock_encrypt_len and returns that total. No error is raised for the early return.

name: aes_gcm_siv_decrypt
prose: AES-GCM-SIV decryption of len bytes from in to out, and computation of the tag that the plaintext should have; it does not itself compare the tag. Precondition: ctx holds the derived keys, nonce, the user-supplied tag (user_tag), the AAD (aad, aad_len) and the ecb cipher context; in and out have len bytes. It clears generated_tag first. It returns 0 without decrypting if the context has already been used to decrypt (used_dec) and speed mode is off, or if len exceeds 2^36. Otherwise it forms the CTR initial block from user_tag with the top bit of its last byte set, decrypts in to out with the 32-bit counter routine, then computes the POLYVAL hash over the AAD (padded to 16 bytes), the decrypted data (last partial block zero-padded) and the bit lengths of AAD and data, XORs in the nonce, clears the top bit of the last byte, and encrypts the result with AES-ECB into ctx->tag (the locally computed S_s block is only an intermediate). generated_tag is set to 1 if the decryption and tag encryption succeeded, used_dec is set to 1 whether or not an error occurred, and the function returns 1 on success and 0 if the CTR routine or the ECB encryption failed. The plaintext is already in out when it returns; checking ctx->tag against user_tag is done elsewhere.

Original reviewer right: the computed tag is stored in ctx->tag (258-260) and S_s is only a local. Round-15 reviewer wrong for this function: it has no tag-mismatch return, it returns !error (263) and the comparison is not here.

name: aes_ocb_block_update_internal
prose: Feeds inl bytes of in through the AES-OCB block routine ciph in whole 16-byte blocks, keeping any partial block in buf (with fill count *bufsz). It is used for both data (out non-NULL) and AAD (out NULL, with the AAD buffer). Precondition: buf holds AES_BLOCK_SIZE bytes, *bufsz <= 16; outsize is the room in out. If a partial block is buffered it first tops it up from in (ossl_cipher_fillblock); when that fills a block, it requires outsize >= 16 (else PROV_R_OUTPUT_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL and 0), processes the block with ciph (failure raises PROV_R_CIPHER_OPERATION_FAILED and returns 0), clears *bufsz, counts 16 output bytes and advances out. It then processes the whole blocks that remain in in (requiring outsize to cover the counted bytes, else error 0; ciph failure 0), and stores any trailing partial block in buf via ossl_cipher_trailingdata (its failure returns 0, error already raised). On success *outl is set to the number of bytes counted as processed (bytes written to out for data; for AAD, the AAD bytes consumed, since nothing is written) and the return value is 1 only if all input was consumed (inl == 0 at the end). *outl is not set on any failure path.

name: chacha20_poly1305_aead_cipher
prose: Single entry point of the ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD for AAD, data and final calls (and TLS records). Precondition: bctx holds a PROV_CHACHA20_POLY1305_CTX; outl is non-NULL; in/out/inl select the call type: in != NULL and out == NULL is AAD; in != NULL and out != NULL is data; in == NULL is the explicit final. If the MAC has not been started: in TLS mode (a TLS payload length is set) with out non-NULL it returns 0 when inl is not payload length + 16 (without setting *outl) and otherwise, unless built for small footprint, returns the result of chacha20_poly1305_tls_cipher; else it derives the Poly1305 key from block 0 of the ChaCha20 stream, starts the MAC, resets counters and lengths, and in TLS mode absorbs the TLS AAD. AAD calls feed the MAC, add to the AAD length and finish with *outl = inl although nothing is written. Data calls first pad out the AAD to a block, require inl equal to payload length + 16 in TLS mode (otherwise error exit with *outl = 0 and result 0), and encrypt-then-MAC (encrypt) or MAC-then-decrypt (decrypt) plen bytes, advancing in and out. A final or TLS tag step (when in is NULL or inl differs from plen) pads the data, appends the lengths to the MAC and finishes it: when encrypting the tag is stored in ctx->tag and, for an appended-tag record, copied to out; when decrypting with an appended tag a mismatch zeroes the plen output bytes and takes the error exit with result 0, and a match strips the tag from inl; for an explicit final on decryption the computed tag is compared with the stored tag (mismatch gives the error exit with result 0). On success *outl is set to inl as it stands (for appended-tag decryption the input length minus 16, for other calls the number of bytes processed or consumed) and the result is 1; on the error exit *outl is 0 and the result is 0.

name: tdes_init
prose: Common initialisation for triple-DES encrypt and decrypt contexts. Precondition: vctx is a PROV_CIPHER_CTX of a TDES cipher; key and iv may each be NULL (to keep the previous ones); keylen/ivlen describe them. Returns 0 at once if the provider is not running. Before any other check it resets the partial-block state (num and bufsz to 0) and stores the direction ctx->enc = enc, so these changes remain even if a later step fails. If iv is non-NULL it installs it with ossl_cipher_generic_initiv (failure returns 0, an IV length problem being checked there). If iv is NULL and an IV had been set earlier in CBC, CFB or OFB mode, the working IV is reset from the original IV. If key is non-NULL its length must equal ctx->keylen (else PROV_R_INVALID_KEY_LENGTH and 0), the hardware init sets the key schedule (failure returns 0) and key_set is set to 1. It then applies params through ossl_tdes_set_ctx_params (failure returns 0), and in FIPS builds checks that encryption is approved (failure returns 0). Returns 1 on success, which also happens when key and iv are both NULL (nothing is then installed).

name: ossl_cipher_generic_block_final
prose: Finishes a block-cipher operation by processing the last buffered data. Precondition: vctx is a PROV_CIPHER_CTX; out has outsize bytes; outl is non-NULL. Returns 0 if the provider is not running, 0 with PROV_R_NO_KEY_SET if no key was set, and 0 with PROV_R_CIPHER_OPERATION_FAILED for a TLS-mode context (a TLS-mode context is rejected by this function). Encrypting: with padding enabled it pads whatever number of bytes is buffered (any length from 0 to blocksize-1) to a full block; without padding, an empty buffer gives *outl = 0 and 1, and a buffer that is not exactly one block gives PROV_R_WRONG_FINAL_BLOCK_LENGTH and 0. It then needs outsize >= blocksize (else PROV_R_OUTPUT_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL and 0), encrypts that block into out (failure PROV_R_CIPHER_OPERATION_FAILED, 0), clears bufsz, sets *outl to the block size and returns 1. Decrypting: the buffer must hold exactly one block, except that an empty buffer without padding returns *outl = 0 and 1; any other length raises PROV_R_WRONG_FINAL_BLOCK_LENGTH and returns 0. It decrypts that block in place (failure 0), removes the padding when padding is enabled (failure 0 with the error already raised by the unpad routine), requires outsize to cover the remaining bytes (else PROV_R_OUTPUT_BUFFER_TOO_SMALL and 0), copies them to out, sets *outl to their count, clears bufsz and returns 1. *outl is not set on failure.

name: ccm_cipher_internal
prose: Common AES-CCM cipher entry point covering the message-length, AAD, data and final steps (and TLS records). Precondition: ctx holds the CCM context; padlen is non-NULL. Returns 0 (without setting *padlen) if no key was set. If a TLS AAD was set (tls_aad_len initialised) it returns the result of ccm_tls_cipher, which works in place on a record with 8-byte explicit IV and tag, copies the explicit IV on encryption, sets the CCM IV and message length (so len_set becomes 1), sets the saved AAD, encrypts or decrypts, and reports the output length in *padlen; it does not reset iv_set, tag_set or len_set after a TLS decryption. In the normal path: in == NULL with out != NULL (final, which returns no data) returns 1 with *padlen = 0; otherwise the IV must be set (else error exit). With out == NULL: in == NULL passes the message length len to ccm_set_iv (sets len_set); in != NULL is AAD, which needs the message length to be set when len is non-zero, and is fed to setaad. With out != NULL: if the length is not yet set it is set from len; when encrypting it runs auth_encrypt and sets tag_set; when decrypting the tag must already be set, it runs auth_decrypt against the stored tag and then clears iv_set, tag_set and len_set. A failing step goes to the error exit. On success *padlen = len for AAD, length or data calls, and 1 is returned; on the error exit *padlen = 0 and 0 is returned.

name: gcm_init
prose: Common initialisation of an AES-GCM context for encryption or decryption. Precondition: vctx is a PROV_GCM_CTX; iv and key may each be NULL to leave the current ones unchanged; params may carry further settings. Returns 0 if the provider is not running. It stores the direction ctx->enc = enc before checking anything else, so this change persists even if a later step fails. If iv is non-NULL its length must be between 1 and the size of the internal IV buffer (else PROV_R_INVALID_IV_LENGTH and 0); it is then copied into the context, ivlen is updated and the IV state becomes buffered. If key is non-NULL its length must equal ctx->keylen (else PROV_R_INVALID_KEY_LENGTH and 0), the hardware setkey installs the key (failure returns 0) and the TLS record counter is reset to 0.
